audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Gragas, Skill, Kayle, Kayle, Gragas... while the content whys under those same rows say the opposite: whys[0] calls level 1 'a wash', and whys[1], whys[2] and whys[3] all say Gragas wins levels 2 through 5.
audit.why: Kayle is melee with one point of W until 6; Drunken Rage's damage reduction plus Happy Hour out-sustain her chip, and Body Slam into the Q pool out-bursts anything she can answer.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 flipped in both layers as one atomic group to Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Gragas — matching the packet chart and the already-audited Gragas-side page exactly — with ratings and all four phases[].why lines rewritten to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page told the reader to 'track Body Slam' in five places without ever giving its cooldown, so there was no way to know how long the punish window lasts.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 — a long cooldown for a champion whose only gap-closer it is. That number is what makes 'fight when it is down' actionable.
audit.corrected: 14s at rank 1 written into phases[1].why, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it: the page never names a single Gragas ability, writing 'his E body-slam', 'Q pool' and 'W damage reduction' instead. The anti-heal line also never said what is doing the healing.
audit.why: Happy Hour (P) heals on every skill use, which is exactly why Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades here — the _missing entry for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Body Slam, Drunken Rage and Happy Hour now appear by name in the phases, the do's, the interactions block and the itemization line.

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flagged "Divine Ascent's" in wants.you[0]; Divine Ascent is Kayle's real passive name, so it is a false positive and the line was left alone.

edits.before: You are the weakest level 1 in the game — pay rent quietly. Identify how Gragas contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — his Body Slam is not up yet, so last-hit at Q range and set the wave up quietly: you are the weakest level 1 in the game.

edits.before: E-poke softens his step-ups while you scale. Only take the trade when Gragas's Body Slam is down.
edits.after: Body Slam (14s) into the Q pool plus a W-empowered auto out-bursts you — concede the trade and farm.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gragas must walk into your range.
edits.after: Drunken Rage's damage reduction tanks your Q and Happy Hour out-sustains one point of W — give nothing here.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Body Slam's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: He still wins attrition through damage reduction and Happy Hour heals while you are melee and pre-6 — farm safe, do not contest.

edits.before: His engage. Survive it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Body Slam (E) is 14s at rank 1 — step up only when it is down.

edits.before: Track Gragas's Body Slam: His engage. Survive it. When it is down — E-poke + scale.
edits.after: Track Body Slam (E, 14s): his only gap-closer. When it is down — E-poke and scale.

edits.before: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Core: Nashor's Tooth  (the ramp begins), then Riftmaker / Rabadon's Deathcap; boots Mercury's Treads. Anti-heal (Oblivion Orb / Executioner's) early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Core: Nashor's Tooth (the ramp begins), then Riftmaker / Rabadon's Deathcap; boots Mercury's Treads. Anti-heal (Oblivion Orb / Executioner's) early — Happy Hour (P) heals off your chip.

notes: Chart flipped as one atomic group in both layers to Skill/Gragas/Gragas/Gragas/Gragas/Kayle/Kayle, identical to the packet chart and the Gragas-side audit.
